findings.title: Spring-qualified mud
findings.claim: The adjective makes the dark muddy quality belong to the spring as its qualifier.
findings.mechanism: Genitive indefinite agreement between hamiʾatin and aynin binds the material quality to the spring noun rather than to the sun.
findings.reader_payoff: The murk becomes a property of the physical medium through which the setting is seen.
findings.containment: The finding remains the ordinary muddy-spring scene and does not turn the adjective into a claim about the sun.

epistemic.reason: The cited focus grammar and lexical supports directly state the agreement and its local effect.

findings.title: Material horizon
findings.claim: The spring is rendered as dark, altered sediment, giving the western horizon a concrete material density.
findings.mechanism: The adjective's supplied rare mud and creation-clay pressure meets its local spring agreement, so darkness is perceived as altered matter rather than a free-floating mood.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the horizon as a physical muddy medium.
findings.containment: The local adjective still qualifies the spring; the wider creation-mud association is a bounded pressure, not a replacement scene.

epistemic.reason: The local lexical claim is anchored, while the rare creation-mud association is explicitly qualified in the cited support.

findings.title: Roughened adjective
findings.claim: The hamza gives the muddy qualifier an audible catch that suits its rough material image.

findings.reader_payoff: The sound lets the physical roughness of the qualifier be heard as well as understood.
findings.containment: This is an audible coloring of the established adjective, not a new lexical sense.

epistemic.reason: A citable phonetic support directly records the hamza effect and its bounded image.

findings.title: Sediment and heat
findings.claim: The supplied variant pressure lets the muddy spring reading remain in place while heat is heard beside it.
findings.mechanism: The hamza-bearing form and the cited hot active-participle variant attach two physical pressures to the same spring description without erasing the first.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold dark sediment and heat together in the scene.
findings.containment: The heat is variant-supported qualification; it does not displace the muddy form or assert a separate event.

epistemic.reason: The cited qiraat support explicitly contrasts the two forms and preserves their bounded relation.

findings.title: Second finding clause

findings.mechanism: The coordinating wa links two completed finding clauses instead of reducing the people to a detail inside the first scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah visibly opens a new discovery after the horizon event.
findings.containment: The second discovery remains coordinated with the first; it does not cancel the physical sunset scene.

epistemic.reason: The cited focus grammar support directly identifies the coordination.

findings.title: Scene-bound coordination

findings.mechanism: The additive conjunction joins the encounter to the preceding setting without swallowing the people into the spring description.

findings.containment: The relation is scene-bound coordination, not a claim that the people are inside the spring.

epistemic.reason: The cited support records additive coordination with circumstantial pressure rather than a stronger containment claim.
